question: Where is the Nuclear Fuel Complex of India situated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyderabad**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC)** of India is located in **Hyderabad**, Telangana.
 
• Established in **1971**, NFC is a major industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), Government of India.
 
• The complex is responsible for the supply of nuclear fuel bundles and reactor core components for all the nuclear power reactors operating in India.
 
• NFC plays a critical role in India's nuclear power generation program and the production of heavy water reactors and pressurized heavy water reactors.
 
• The facility also manufactures zirconium alloy cladding tubes and other structural materials required for the nuclear power reactors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyderabad** is the capital city of the Indian state of Telangana and is known for its rich history, culture, and landmarks such as the Charminar.
 
• The city is a major center for the technology industry, with numerous multinational companies having their offices there.
 
• Hyderabad is also known for its educational institutions, including the University of Hyderabad and the Indian School of Business.
 
• The city's economy is driven by sectors such as information technology, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology.
 
• Hyderabad has a well-developed infrastructure and is connected to other major cities through its international airport and extensive rail and road networks.
